newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid stocks end soggy with bonds, utilities mixed.
newsitem.headline: Madrid stocks end soggy with bonds, utilities mixed.

text.p: Madrid stocks closed a tad lower on Thursday, in line with weaker bonds and early losses on Wall Street, dealers said.
The general index down 1.09 points, 0.27 percent, to 404.18 and the Ibex fell 13.93 points, 0.3 percent, to 4,663.87.
Dealers focused on November CPI and a Bank of Spain repo auction tomorrow, with expectations of a rate cut just outweighing predictions for no move.
Spanish inflation is expected to have risen 0.0-0.2 percent in November from the previous month, with the year-on-year rate seen at 3.2-3.4 percent from 3.5 percent in October.
Utilities were at the centre of trade after a protocol agreeing a framework for competition was signed late Wednesday.
Iberdrola shed 40 pesetas to 1,585, Cantabrico -which refused to sign the agreement- fell 85 pesetas to 4,405. Endesa rose 80 pesetas to 8,570 and Fenosa added 15 pesetas to 1,065.

Fenosa and Endesa gained ground as both are expected to be helped by the new framework, dealers said. Endesa was also bouyant ahead of the placement of up to 25 percent of its share capital on the market sometime mid-1997.
